text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The director of customs, Saul Kaulinge, has been accused of not declaring his interests in a business which sells mostly clothing imported from Asia. He is also alleged to have used his authority to clear the goods and not paid tax nor duty on the wares. Kaulinge has denied the allegations.
- Prime Minister Hage Geingob had defended the planned amendment of the Local Authorities Act which will provide for the party list system to be used in December's local elections.

- Almost a million hectares along Namibia's coastline will be opened up for offshore diamond mining within the next ten years. Applications will be considered for the geological and environmental appraisal of at least 15 blocks and for proposed exploration programmes.

- Fisheries experts and scientists from 12 countries will meet on April 3 in Walvis Bay at the invitation of Namibia, South Africa and Angola to discuss an ambitious programme for the use of marine resources. The three countries share the marine environment of the Benguela current.
